title: Accepted TCP socket does not inherit listener TCP_KEEPIDLE
mechanism: StreamSocket::new_accepted builds the accepted socket's options from OptionSet::new and copies only keepalive enablement and interval and TCP_NODELAY (from the raw socket or the listener), so a TCP_KEEPIDLE value set on the listener stays at the default on the accepted socket.
contract: On Linux the accepted socket reports the TCP_KEEPIDLE value set on the listener before the connection arrived (the saved Linux 6.18 run read 17 on both), while accept(2) notes that file status flags such as O_NONBLOCK are not inherited.
observed: By source reading at the pin (not run): getsockopt(TCP_KEEPIDLE) on the accepted socket returns the default instead of the listener's 17.

repro.how_to_run: Run `make static` in repro/ on x86-64 Linux, copy bin/abi_probe into an Asterinas guest, and run `abi_probe <case>` for tcp_accept_keepidle, tcp_accept_flags. repro/README.md gives the saved Linux output.

caveats: SOURCE LEAD, Asterinas NOT_RUN. Option-state inheritance only. Asterinas does not use keep_idle for keepalive timing at the pin (TODO in do_tcp_setsockopt), so there is no packet-timing evidence.
